# Atrax v0 complete agent reference

Atrax creates, runs, deploys, inspects, and debugs small full-stack apps from one CLI. v0 deploys public Cloudflare Workers with Static Assets and one D1 database.

Read-only agent onboarding: `curl -fsSL https://atrax.run/agent`

## Install

Requires Node.js 22.13 or newer and an authenticated Wrangler session.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rishabhsai/tarantula.git
cd tarantula
npm install
npm link
atrax doctor --json
```

## Create and deploy

```bash
atrax new open-chat --template chat
cd open-chat
atrax dev
atrax plan --json
atrax deploy --json
atrax inspect --json
atrax drift --json
atrax logs
```

The chat is public. Anyone with the URL can read and post.

## CLI

- `atrax new <name> --template chat`
- `atrax dev [--port 8787]`
- `atrax deploy [--json]`
- `atrax deploy --dry-run`
- `atrax deploy --instant`
- `atrax claim <token> [--json]`
- `atrax plan [--json]`
- `atrax drift [--json]`
- `atrax inspect [--json]`
- `atrax logs [--json]`
- `atrax doctor [--json]`
- `atrax share add <email> [--json]`
- `atrax share list [--json]`
- `atrax share remove <email> [--json]`

Finite JSON commands return one object with `schemaVersion: 1`. `logs --json` is a long-running Wrangler NDJSON event stream. Errors return a non-zero exit code, and unknown flags fail before mutation.

`plan` is read-only. It emits `{ schemaVersion, status: "planned" | "blocked", name, changes, actions[], migrations: { pending[] }, conflicts[] }`, where each action is `{ product, resource, action, reason }` with an action of create, recreate, update, keep, apply, or none.

`drift` is read-only and requires a lockfile. It emits `{ schemaVersion, status: "clean" | "drifted", name, checks[] }`, where each check is `{ check, expected, observed, result }` with a result of ok, drift, or unknown. Checks cover account, worker, deployment, url, tables, and migrations.

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` error including a blocked plan, `2` only from `drift` when the provider no longer matches the lockfile.

## Instant hosting

`atrax deploy` uses Atrax instant hosting when no Cloudflare account is detected; `--instant` forces it. The app runs on Atrax's own Cloudflare account as one Worker plus one D1 database, on a real public `https://i-<appId>....workers.dev` URL. The claim token is printed exactly once, by the deploy that mints it: it is never written to disk and redeploys never reprint it. An unclaimed app is deleted 30 days after creation; `atrax claim <token>` keeps the same URL and clears the expiry.

```json
{ "schemaVersion": 1, "status": "deployed", "mode": "instant", "name": "open-chat",
  "url": "https://i-3f9a2c81be.<subdomain>.workers.dev", "appId": "3f9a2c81be",
  "access": "public", "claimToken": "...", "expiresAt": 1790000000000,
  "resources": { "tables": { "name": "i-3f9a2c81be-tables" } } }
```

```json
{ "schemaVersion": 1, "status": "claimed", "appId": "3f9a2c81be",
  "url": "https://i-3f9a2c81be.<subdomain>.workers.dev" }
```

`claimToken` and `expiresAt` (epoch milliseconds) appear only on the deploy that creates the app. Local state lives in `.atrax/instant.json` (mode 0600, gitignored) as `{ appId, manageToken, url }`, and `atrax.lock.json` records `{ "provider": "atrax-instant", "mode": "instant", "appId", "worker": { "name", "url" } }`. Creates are capped at 10 per day per IP. `inspect`, `logs`, `plan`, and `drift` refuse instant locks, since each reads Cloudflare through Wrangler against an account the deployer does not have.

`access` is `"public"` or `"shared"` and names who can open the URL; the human output prints the same fact in one line under the URL, and a public first deploy appends the `atrax claim <token>` line to it. Instant hosting serves both visibilities: a `"visibility": "shared"` app deploys normally, instant hosting generates that app's `DOOR_SESSION_SECRET` itself once and never returns it, and `atrax share` manages members through Atrax instead of the caller's Cloudflare account. The commands, the payloads, and the `door_members` table are the same on both paths.

## Shared visibility

`visibility` accepts `"public"` (default, unchanged) or `"shared"`. A shared app is gated inside the template Worker by a small Door module. Deploy provisions the `DOOR_SESSION_SECRET` Worker secret once and records `"door": { "secretProvisioned": true }` in the lockfile; the secret is never written to disk.

`atrax share add <email>` stores a hashed, single-use, 14-day invite token in the app's own `door_members` D1 table and returns the invite URL; an instant lock routes the same command through Atrax instant hosting. `share list` reports each member as joined, invited, or expired. `share remove` deletes the row. Visiting `/.door/join?token=...` sets a 30-day HMAC-signed `__door_session` cookie and redirects to `/`. `/.door/whoami` returns the signed-in member. `/.well-known/*` stays reachable so readiness checks work. Every other request without a valid session gets a 401 invitation page.

```json
{ "schemaVersion": 1, "status": "invited", "email": "ana@example.com",
  "inviteUrl": "https://open-chat...workers.dev/.door/join?token=...", "expiresAt": 1790000000000 }
```

This is the Door alpha slice, not the Door product. There are no roles, teams, email delivery, or central session revocation. `plan` reports a `door / session-secret` action and `drift` adds a `door` check for shared apps.

## App contract

`atrax.json` is the provider-neutral desired architecture. `atrax.lock.json` records stable non-secret resource identities and is safe to commit; it is not the future authoritative infrastructure state. Do not edit `.atrax/wrangler.jsonc`; Atrax generates it as a disposable provider artifact. Declared files must remain inside the app and may not contain symlinks.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "name": "open-chat",
  "visibility": "public",
  "web": {
    "entry": "src/worker.js",
    "assets": "public",
    "health": "/.well-known/atrax.json"
  },
  "tables": { "migrations": "migrations" }
}
```

`visibility` accepts `"public"` or `"shared"`. Nothing else validates.

## Infrastructure model

Atrax products are the public abstraction. Infrastructure-as-code is an internal reconciliation engine. `plan` and `drift` work today against the single implicit v0 environment. The planned model adds `stacks/dev.json` and `stacks/prod.json` for environment intent, remote locked state for authoritative observations and drift metadata, and stack-aware `plan`, `deploy`, and `drift`.

Stateful infrastructure, immutable releases, and Switchboard secret/connection references have separate lifecycles. Provider engines remain replaceable implementation details.

## Available products

Launchpad v0 runs locally, deploys Worker and Static Assets, waits for readiness, keeps a stable workers.dev URL, inspects deployment state, and streams logs.

Tables v0 provisions D1, applies ordered local and remote migrations, keeps the binding across releases, and reports database state.

## Planned products

Door will own guest identity, sign-in, sharing, teams, roles, and app identity. An alpha slice ships today: shared visibility with invite links via `atrax share`.

Library will own files and company knowledge, including collections, provenance, freshness, and permission-aware retrieval. It will not store credentials or perform actions.

Switchboard will own the company vault, OAuth connections, typed tools, scoped grants, app-to-app capabilities, and the action ledger. It will not store company knowledge.

Loops will own declared webhooks, schedules, queues, background jobs, and operational agents with durable execution semantics. Ordinary Worker request handlers remain part of an app's web runtime until they opt into one `loop({ on, run, tools?, approve? })` contract.

## Security

Cloudflare credentials remain in Wrangler. Account mismatch, lock-name mismatch, and unlocked Worker or D1 collisions fail before mutation. The chat validates input on the server, caps posts at 4 KiB and 12 per IP per minute, retains 500 messages, and renders messages with `textContent`. Public access is intentional and stated in the generated app.

Private access, vaulted third-party connections, approval binding, compliance reports, backups and export, custom domains, previews, rollback, and a hosted control panel are not available in v0.

## Machine entrypoints

- `/docs.json`
- `/llms.txt`
- `/llms-full.txt`
- `/schema/v0.json`
- `/.well-known/atrax.json` on generated apps
